chapter: Early life and the plantation brass band
title: The plantation brass band: parades, size, instruments, breakup
summary: The band paraded for the masons at Woodland and nearby. It had ten pieces: cornets, trombones, altos, baritone, bass and drums, no clarinet. It broke up as the old players died or left, and Sonny Henry is recalled.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Do you remember anything else about your brass band? Did they have parades down there when you were young?
Yeah. I played music down there, who they are, in the parades down there. They had the mason down there. But the mason was at Woodland.

At a place below us called Woodland. I've heard of that. And we used to go down there and play the for rids and things. Bring them up further this way to the church and carry them back and dismiss them. And we'd come back on the dairy.
Magnolia plantation was near it. It was below that. It was down below. Yes, below that.
Was it below Woodland too then? Magnolia? Uh-huh. Yeah. It was farther down the river. Sure. Sure, farther down. Do you remember how many you had in the band, about how big a band it was?
Ten pieces. How many trombones and how many cornets about do you remember?
We had three cornets. We had three cornets and we had two trombones. But there was key trombones. Yes.
Have alto horn and baritone or what else? Yeah.

We had solo alto and we had baritone and we had bass too. We had a first alto in our band. Bass drum and snare drum. Any clarinet? No. No clarinet? No. We didn't have no clarinet. We had a first tenor in our band. A brass instrument? Yes.
Something like a baritone was that?
Yes. That's right. How long did you play down in that band? When did you come up to New Orleans?
I played in that band until it broke up. You finally broke up then? Yes. And it broke up.
And you remember when that was? So many old heads would play in there and died out and went to different places and the band just went to finish.
Oh, do you remember Sonny Henry down that way? That's right. We knew him very well. Yes, that's right.
Sonny Henry. He died right up here. Last Christmas time, about January he died. Yeah, Sonny Henry. Sonny Henry, the field form, anarchy, the Irish bone. They all come from the same house.
